note: The assert(false)-else guard, in the two positions the multi-result branch node missed. Both used to compile to a script that ran to the end and left a falsy top of stack, because the state continuation committed the PRE-call value of the written property while the SDK serialised the post-call one. Every expectedState below is derived from the source by hand, not from anything the compiler produced, so a continuation that commits stale state fails here even though the arms are balanced and the script is well-formed.

spends.note: P0-1: guarded single-property write. n=5 > 0 takes the then-arm, so count = 0 + 5 = 5; a and b are untouched. The stale-slot bug committed count = 0 here.
P0-1 negative: n=0 is not > 0, so the else-arm's assert(false) must abort. The guard has to keep rejecting after the fix, not merely start accepting.
P0-2: the dispatch chain inside a loop body, sel=0. The loop is unrolled twice and both iterations take the first arm, so a = 7 and b is never written.
P0-2, the other arm: sel=1 writes b = 9 in both unrolled iterations and leaves a at 0. Two arms writing DIFFERENT property sets is the shape the multi-result node exists to fix.
P0-2 negative: an out-of-range selector must abort on the chain's terminal assert(false) rather than produce a spendable no-op continuation (the C20 funds-safety property, here inside a loop).
